A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
plant size and N(M) have a strong impact on biomass allocation to foliage, but their effects on foliar structure and function can be independent.
the scaling of leaf structure and function, and biomass allocation, is a complex trait controlled by both internal plant nitrogen content and tree height.
the leaf and whole-plant parameters are controlled by N and H, but that the degree of control differs among species.
The main takeaway from our work is that
plant size and internal nitrogen content are two major determinants of the foliar structure, photosynthetic activity and biomass allocation.

the scaling patterns in leaf and plant characteristics are not simply a consequence of the modified light availabilities, but are more likely to reflect the combined effects of the modified nutrient availability and the modified light availabilites on the growth rate of the whole plant.
the effects of N and H on leaf structure and physiology are not necessarily additive, but can also be antagonistic.
